report.incidentSummary: On the morning of 2026-10-05, multiple users reported duplicate bank debits for their scheduled SIP instalments. Investigation revealed that configuration change CHG-48217, applied on 2026-10-04 at 18:40 IST (13:10 UTC), had reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms. During the morning SIP debit batch (00:30 UTC to 02:30 UTC / 06:00 IST to 08:00 IST), debit presentations to partner bank Kaveri that took longer than 3000ms timed out prematurely on debit-worker. Configured to resubmit upon confirmation timeout, debit-worker resubmitted 2,236 debits under new debit IDs. Kaveri bank processed both the initial and resubmitted debit requests, generating confirmed duplicate debits across mandates.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout (bank.confirm_timeout_ms) from 8000ms to 3000ms, creating a timeout mismatch against partner bank processing times and bank-connector's 8000ms upstream timeout. Debits against Kaveri bank taking longer than 3000ms timed out prematurely on debit-worker, triggering automated resubmissions with distinct debit IDs that Kaveri bank fulfilled twice.

hypotheses.cause: Config change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms, causing premature client timeouts and automated resubmissions against Kaveri bank which subsequently processed both debit attempts.
hypotheses.rationale: Evidence directly confirms CHG-48217 reduced the timeout to 3000ms prior to the batch run. During the batch run, debit-worker logged 2,236 warnings of no confirmation within 3000ms specifically on Kaveri bank and resubmitted them. Duplicate-check logs later confirmed multiple mandates had two debited transactions with separate debit IDs.

hypotheses.cause: Partner bank Kaveri suffered an external latency degradation during the morning batch run, driving response times past baseline and causing debit-worker timeouts and retries.
hypotheses.rationale: While Kaveri bank responses frequently exceeded 3000ms, the primary fault lies in the artificial reduction of the confirmation timeout to 3000ms on debit-worker while bank-connector still had an 8000ms timeout budget. Normal bank debit processing latency can naturally range between 3s and 8s.

facts.statement: Configuration change CHG-48217 was applied to debit-worker on 2026-10-04T13:10:00.000Z (18:40 IST), lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms.

debit-worker has a synchronous dependency on bank-connector with retries=2 and resubmits debits if no confirmation is received within the timeout, whereas bank-connector uses an 8000ms timeout towards bank-apis.
job-scheduler executed the sip-debit-batch job exactly once between 2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z and 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z under run ID run_c511c4c2.

Between 2026-10-05T00:50:00.000Z and 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z, debit-worker experienced elevated retries peaking at 280.3 retries/min, isolated specifically to Kaveri bank (up to 268.5 retries/min) while other partner banks remained below 6 retries/min.
debit-worker recorded 2,236 warning logs between 00:50:01 UTC and 02:34:59 UTC stating 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)' specifically targeting Kaveri bank.

Starting at 2026-10-05T02:40:35.986Z (08:10:35 IST), debit-worker logged 244 duplicate-check ERROR entries indicating mandates on Kaveri bank had 2 confirmed debits with distinct debit IDs for instalment 2026-10-05.
mf-order-service version 4.1.0 (CHG-48225) was deployed on 2026-10-05T03:45:00.000Z (09:15 IST), and contains no logs matching debit processing events.

inferences.statement: The deployment of mf-order-service at 09:15 IST did not cause the duplicate debits, as debit-worker began logging duplicate debits at 08:10 IST and user tickets began at ~09:00 IST.

Lowering debit-worker's confirmation timeout to 3000ms while bank-connector still waits up to 8000ms created a window where in-flight bank transactions taking between 3s and 8s were aborted prematurely by debit-worker and resubmitted.
Kaveri bank processed both the original and resubmitted debit requests because the resubmissions were issued under distinct debit IDs without idempotency protection across retries.

assumptions.statement: Kaveri bank API does not enforce idempotency on debit requests when distinct debit IDs are sent for the same mandate instalment.
Kaveri bank debit confirmation responses historically and normally take between 3000ms and 8000ms during peak batch execution.

timeline.event: Config change CHG-48217 applied to debit-worker, lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms.
job-scheduler starts sip-debit-batch run_c511c4c2.
debit-worker begins timing out at 3000ms on Kaveri bank requests and initiates 2,236 automated resubmissions (attempt 2).
job-scheduler finishes sip-debit-batch run_c511c4c2 successfully.
debit-worker duplicate-check starts logging ERROR lines for mandates with 2 confirmed debits on Kaveri bank.
Customers receive duplicate bank SMS notifications and begin raising support tickets.
mf-order-service v4.1.0 deployed (CHG-48225).

confidence.rationale: There is a direct, verified causal chain connecting CHG-48217's 3000ms timeout change, the 2,236 log entries documenting 3000ms timeouts and retries on Kaveri bank, and the subsequent duplicate confirmed debits identified by debit-worker's duplicate-check logic.

gaps.description: Historical p95/p99 latency distribution for Kaveri bank debit confirmations prior to CHG-48217 was not captured.
gaps.impact: Low; does not prevent establishing that the 3000ms timeout prematurely cut off requests that were still fulfilled.

gaps.description: bank-connector metric query for timeout_count returned partial completeness.
gaps.impact: Negligible; debit-worker logs and retry metrics conclusively document the timeouts and resubmission volume.

recommendedActions.action: Revert debit-worker's bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 3000ms back to at least 8000ms (matching or exceeding bank-connector's timeout).
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents debit-worker from aborting and resubmitting debit requests while bank-connector and partner bank APIs are still processing them.
recommendedActions.verification: Check debit-worker runtime configuration to verify bank.confirm_timeout_ms is >= 8000ms, and verify retry_count on Kaveri bank drops to baseline during batch runs.

recommendedActions.action: Initiate reconciliation and automated refund processing for all Kaveri bank mandates flagged with duplicate confirmed debits for instalment 2026-10-05.
recommendedActions.rationale: Remediates user impact from double deductions reported by customers and logged by duplicate-check.
recommendedActions.verification: Query debit-worker duplicate-check logs and bank settlement files to confirm all secondary debit transactions have corresponding reversal/refund records.

recommendedActions.action: Implement end-to-end idempotency keys on debit presentations so that retries reuse the same external bank transaction reference rather than generating new debit IDs.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures that even if debit-worker times out and retries, partner banks reject or de-duplicate duplicate presentation attempts.
recommendedActions.verification: Perform staging integration testing where bank-connector introduces synthetic delays, confirming retried debits return identical bank debit IDs without duplicate ledger deductions.

findings.summary: job-scheduler executed the sip-debit-batch job exactly once between 00:30:00 UTC and 02:30:00 UTC (run_c511c4c2). message-queue maintained stable queue depth with routine consumer rebalances, and mf-order-service showed normal order creation metrics without duplicate debit event processing. The root cause of duplicate debits is not in upstream scheduling or queue orchestration, pointing to the downstream debit execution layer (debit-worker / bank-connector).

observations.statement: job-scheduler triggered the sip-debit-batch job exactly once during the investigation window (run_c511c4c2 started at 2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z and completed successfully at 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z).

message-queue queue_depth was steady throughout the window (mean 122.2, min 112.3, max 133.5 messages), with normal periodic rebalancing of consumer groups (order-events, notif-workers, kyc-hooks) and no abnormal backlog or queue spikes.

mf-order-service logs show standard creation of SIP instalment orders and lumpsum purchases; queries filtering for 'debit' returned zero records, indicating mf-order-service does not process debit events directly.
mf-order-service mf_orders_per_min followed a smooth, expected morning volume ramp from ~49 orders/min at 00:15Z to ~660 orders/min around 04:00Z without sudden anomalous spikes.

Upstream orchestration and messaging did not trigger duplicate job runs or re-process duplicate order debit events; the root cause of the duplicate debits is downstream within the debit execution layer (debit-worker and/or bank-connector).

# Investigation report: SIP instalments debited twice

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.85 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
On the morning of 2026-10-05, multiple users reported duplicate bank debits for their scheduled SIP instalments. Investigation revealed that configuration change CHG-48217, applied on 2026-10-04 at 18:40 IST (13:10 UTC), had reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms. During the morning SIP debit batch (00:30 UTC to 02:30 UTC / 06:00 IST to 08:00 IST), debit presentations to partner bank Kaveri that took longer than 3000ms timed out prematurely on debit-worker. Configured to resubmit upon confirmation timeout, debit-worker resubmitted 2,236 debits under new debit IDs. Kaveri bank processed both the initial and resubmitted debit requests, generating confirmed duplicate debits across mandates.

**Root cause:** Configuration change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout (bank.confirm_timeout_ms) from 8000ms to 3000ms, creating a timeout mismatch against partner bank processing times and bank-connector's 8000ms upstream timeout. Debits against Kaveri bank taking longer than 3000ms timed out prematurely on debit-worker, triggering automated resubmissions with distinct debit IDs that Kaveri bank fulfilled twice.

## Hypotheses
1. **Config change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms, causing premature client timeouts and automated resubmissions against Kaveri bank which subsequently processed both debit attempts.** — `debit-worker`, config_change, confidence 0.85, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_2, ev_4, ev_10, ev_13, ev_14, ev_16, ev_18] · Contradicting: none
   - Evidence directly confirms CHG-48217 reduced the timeout to 3000ms prior to the batch run. During the batch run, debit-worker logged 2,236 warnings of no confirmation within 3000ms specifically on Kaveri bank and resubmitted them. Duplicate-check logs later confirmed multiple mandates had two debited transactions with separate debit IDs.
2. **Partner bank Kaveri suffered an external latency degradation during the morning batch run, driving response times past baseline and causing debit-worker timeouts and retries.** — `bank-apis`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.15, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_8, ev_10, ev_14] · Contradicting: [ev_4, ev_13, ev_16]
   - While Kaveri bank responses frequently exceeded 3000ms, the primary fault lies in the artificial reduction of the confirmation timeout to 3000ms on debit-worker while bank-connector still had an 8000ms timeout budget. Normal bank debit processing latency can naturally range between 3s and 8s.

## Facts
- Configuration change CHG-48217 was applied to debit-worker on 2026-10-04T13:10:00.000Z (18:40 IST), lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms. [ev_4]
- debit-worker has a synchronous dependency on bank-connector with retries=2 and resubmits debits if no confirmation is received within the timeout, whereas bank-connector uses an 8000ms timeout towards bank-apis. [ev_13]
- job-scheduler executed the sip-debit-batch job exactly once between 2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z and 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z under run ID run_c511c4c2. [ev_1]
- Between 2026-10-05T00:50:00.000Z and 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z, debit-worker experienced elevated retries peaking at 280.3 retries/min, isolated specifically to Kaveri bank (up to 268.5 retries/min) while other partner banks remained below 6 retries/min. [ev_2, ev_10]
- debit-worker recorded 2,236 warning logs between 00:50:01 UTC and 02:34:59 UTC stating 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)' specifically targeting Kaveri bank. [ev_14, ev_16]
- Starting at 2026-10-05T02:40:35.986Z (08:10:35 IST), debit-worker logged 244 duplicate-check ERROR entries indicating mandates on Kaveri bank had 2 confirmed debits with distinct debit IDs for instalment 2026-10-05. [ev_14, ev_18]
- mf-order-service version 4.1.0 (CHG-48225) was deployed on 2026-10-05T03:45:00.000Z (09:15 IST), and contains no logs matching debit processing events. [ev_4, ev_11, ev_12]

## Inferences
- The deployment of mf-order-service at 09:15 IST did not cause the duplicate debits, as debit-worker began logging duplicate debits at 08:10 IST and user tickets began at ~09:00 IST. [ev_4, ev_18]
- Lowering debit-worker's confirmation timeout to 3000ms while bank-connector still waits up to 8000ms created a window where in-flight bank transactions taking between 3s and 8s were aborted prematurely by debit-worker and resubmitted. [ev_4, ev_13, ev_14, ev_16]
- Kaveri bank processed both the original and resubmitted debit requests because the resubmissions were issued under distinct debit IDs without idempotency protection across retries. [ev_14, ev_18]

## Assumptions
- Kaveri bank API does not enforce idempotency on debit requests when distinct debit IDs are sent for the same mandate instalment.
- Kaveri bank debit confirmation responses historically and normally take between 3000ms and 8000ms during peak batch execution.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-04T13:10:00.000Z (18:40 IST)** Config change CHG-48217 applied to debit-worker, lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms. [ev_4]
- **2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z (06:00 IST)** job-scheduler starts sip-debit-batch run_c511c4c2. [ev_1]
- **2026-10-05T00:50:01.000Z (06:20:01 IST)** debit-worker begins timing out at 3000ms on Kaveri bank requests and initiates 2,236 automated resubmissions (attempt 2). [ev_2, ev_10, ev_14, ev_16]
- **2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z (08:00 IST)** job-scheduler finishes sip-debit-batch run_c511c4c2 successfully. [ev_1]
- **2026-10-05T02:40:35.000Z (08:10:35 IST)** debit-worker duplicate-check starts logging ERROR lines for mandates with 2 confirmed debits on Kaveri bank. [ev_14, ev_18]
- **2026-10-05T03:30:00.000Z (09:00 IST)** Customers receive duplicate bank SMS notifications and begin raising support tickets.
- **2026-10-05T03:45:00.000Z (09:15 IST)** mf-order-service v4.1.0 deployed (CHG-48225). [ev_4, ev_11]

## Confidence
0.85: There is a direct, verified causal chain connecting CHG-48217's 3000ms timeout change, the 2,236 log entries documenting 3000ms timeouts and retries on Kaveri bank, and the subsequent duplicate confirmed debits identified by debit-worker's duplicate-check logic.

## Gaps
- Historical p95/p99 latency distribution for Kaveri bank debit confirmations prior to CHG-48217 was not captured. (impact: Low; does not prevent establishing that the 3000ms timeout prematurely cut off requests that were still fulfilled.)
- bank-connector metric query for timeout_count returned partial completeness. (impact: Negligible; debit-worker logs and retry metrics conclusively document the timeouts and resubmission volume.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Revert debit-worker's bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 3000ms back to at least 8000ms (matching or exceeding bank-connector's timeout). [ev_4, ev_13, ev_14, ev_16]
  - Why: Prevents debit-worker from aborting and resubmitting debit requests while bank-connector and partner bank APIs are still processing them.
  - Verify: Check debit-worker runtime configuration to verify bank.confirm_timeout_ms is >= 8000ms, and verify retry_count on Kaveri bank drops to baseline during batch runs.
- **[now]** Initiate reconciliation and automated refund processing for all Kaveri bank mandates flagged with duplicate confirmed debits for instalment 2026-10-05. [ev_14, ev_18]
  - Why: Remediates user impact from double deductions reported by customers and logged by duplicate-check.
  - Verify: Query debit-worker duplicate-check logs and bank settlement files to confirm all secondary debit transactions have corresponding reversal/refund records.
- **[next]** Implement end-to-end idempotency keys on debit presentations so that retries reuse the same external bank transaction reference rather than generating new debit IDs. [ev_13, ev_18]
  - Why: Ensures that even if debit-worker times out and retries, partner banks reject or de-duplicate duplicate presentation attempts.
  - Verify: Perform staging integration testing where bank-connector introduces synthetic delays, confirming retried debits return identical bank debit IDs without duplicate ledger deductions.
